text: In a circle, angles in the same segment are equal to one another. Let $ABCD$ be a circle, and let $BAD$ and $BED$ be angles in the same segment $BAED$. I say that angles $BAD$ and $BED$ are equal to one another.
For let the center of circle $ABCD$ be found [Prop.~3.1], and let it be (at point) $F$.
And since angle $BFD$ is at the center, and $BAD$ at the circumference, and they have the same circumference base $BCD$, angle $BFD$ is thus double $BAD$ [Prop.~3.20].
assertion: angle BFD is double angle BAD

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: they have the same circumference base $BCD$

text: So, for the same (reasons), $BFD$ is also double $BED$.
Thus, in a circle, angles in the same segment are equal to one another. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
